## Highlights

- Standing roles now wake when a project worker finishes, so a released slot can be refilled by the fleet manager without waiting for the next scheduled occurrence. Wake claims are scoped to the project and preserve the native task and review guards. [#4608](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4608)
- Audit-log sealing runs asynchronously after the write path, while the integrity panel and verification checks continue to expose the exact source and chain state. The per-project work lock avoids serializing unrelated automation work behind the audit writer. [#4700](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4700)
- Retained deployment observation is bound to the exact deployment reference before it reads runtime state, keeping recovery evidence tied to the operation it describes. [#4755](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4755)

## Upgrade notes

- Deploy the Tale platform and the managed-deployment CLI together. Tale CLI applies migrations 0168 and 0194 during the normal forward-only rollout; keep the existing backup, retained-release and configuration readback procedure until the new image is serving.
- The autonomous-cycle schedules remain enabled and keep their native admission and per-task start limits. A worker or provider failure is recorded on its task and retried or rerouted according to the current project policy; no OpenRouter fallback is required for the OpenAI subscription workers.
